results.title: How to Solve Reproducibility in ML
results.content: Dataset versioning and change tracking must be recorded to achieve reproducibility. Changes in algorithms, data, environments, parameters, etc are all part of the model building process, and while this is fine, it comes with the difficulty of losing important details. 1. Track changes made in the code, data, and environment during experimentation. * MLflow Tracking automatically tracks and logs parameters, metrics, code versions for each model run and deployment with the mlflow.autolog() function. It also keeps track of all the code and data used during model development. * DVC does data and model versioning by creating metafiles as a pointer to stored datasets, models. An artifact in machine learning is data describing the output of a training process of a fully trained model or in ML terms, a model checkpoint. Managing and storing every model checkpoint is important in reproducibility because artifacts make it easy for models to be replicated and verified by the ML team members. * DVC does data and model versioning by creating metafiles as a pointer to stored datasets, models while storing them on-premises or cloud. Data versioning means keeping track and recording every data change at any instance. ### The Best Data Version Control Tools That Improve Your Workflow With Machine Learning Projects. Every model is a compressed version of the data it was trained on and data changes with time like new training data or changes in existing data make the model obsolete on its predictions, so changes to this must get tracked. * Pachyderm helps you find the data origins, then it tracks and versions it as it is processed during model development. Model registry is a tracking mechanism that records and stores all model metadata, lineage, and versioning logs. As you know ML frameworks are constantly being upgraded, so it is important to store and keep the info of the software version and the environment used in building the model. Just make sure you have tools to track your code and computational environment, and also store your metadata, artifacts, and model versions. results.title: DVC (Data Version Control) Pocket Book | Uplatz Blog
results.content: ### 1) What is DVC? Data Version Control (DVC) brings Git-like versioning to large data, models, and ML pipelines. ### 2) Why DVC? Code in Git, big data in DVC. Metafiles (`.dvc`, `dvc.yaml`, `dvc.lock`) live in Git; actual blobs go to cache/remote. .git/ .dvc/ # cache config data/ # large files tracked by DVC models/ # model artifacts tracked by DVC. Git LFS keeps blobs in Git hosting; DVC uses your object storage (S3/GS/Azure/etc.) and adds pipelines/metrics/experiments—more MLOps features. ### 6) What DVC Tracks. **.dvc** (single file tracking for non-pipeline artifacts), **dvc.yaml** (pipeline), **dvc.lock** (frozen state for reproducibility). git add data/raw.dvc dvc.yaml dvc.lock. dvc stage add -n train -d data -d code -o models python train.py. Produces a `.dvc` metafile and pushes content to cache/remote. dvc add data/raw.csv git add data/ .gitignore git commit -m "Track raw data". # Modify generated file, then: dvc commit data/. Use `dvc get` to fetch a file/dir from another DVC repo; `dvc import` to link and update later; `import-url` for external URLs. dvc get data/iris.csv dvc import data/iris.csv. Answer: They pull code with Git, then run `dvc pull` (with the right remote creds). DVC recreates files from the shared cache/remote. Git for code/metadata; DVC for data. Open PRs with `dvc.lock` changes, push artifacts to remote, reviewers run `dvc pull` locally. Committing big blobs to Git, forgetting `dvc push`, breaking cache links, non-deterministic pipelines, and storing secrets in repo. **1) Why DVC for ML?** Git-native workflows with reproducible pipelines and large-file versioning. **2) How does DVC store data?** Content-addressed cache and a remote (e.g., S3); Git stores only pointers. **3) DVC vs Git LFS?** DVC adds pipelines/experiments/metrics and uses your own object storage. **4) What’s in dvc.yaml?** Stages with *cmd*, *deps*, *outs*, *params*, *metrics*, *plots*. **7) How to share data?** Push to remote; teammates run `dvc pull`. **8) How to compare runs?** `dvc metrics diff` and `dvc plots diff` across commits/experiments. **10) How to pin params?** Store in `params.yaml`; DVC tracks and diffs. **18) Resolve merge conflicts?** Regular Git for code; re-run DVC stages and commit updated `dvc.lock`. **19) What is `dvc.lock`?** Frozen snapshot of exact data/params/deps used in a run.

results.content:
Title: Complete CI -Pipeline — MLOps with Github Actions and DvC | by Basu Verma | Medium
# Complete CI -Pipeline — MLOps with Github Actions and DvC. CI pipeline is to automate the process of machine learning to test, build and package orchestrated experiment whenever there is changes in data, model or source code is committed or pushed. DvC is used to track the change in data and model. 2. Adding of DvC pipeline to track the changes in data and model. 3. Adding of workflow file to run the stages mentioned in dvc yaml file whenever the event is trigger. This will add the given data for tracking with DvC. A **.dvc** file will be generated that contains the metadata. 2. dvc.yaml file:- To define all the stages and corresponding dependencies. ***deps***: the input files required to successfully run that particular stage. The above file on running will generate the ***dvc.lock*** file. The ***dvc.lock*** file will contain the metadata for all the dependents and output files. 1. ci.yaml file: - This file contains all the steps to run on ubuntu provided instance. name: ci-pipelineon: [push]jobs:  CI-Pipeline:    runs-on: [ubuntu-latest]    env:      repo_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}    steps:      - name: Checkout Repo        uses: actions/checkout@v2              - name: Install CML        uses: iterative/setup-cml@v1              - name: Install DVC        uses: iterative/setup-dvc@v1              - name: Setup python        uses: actions/setup-python@v4        with:          python-version: '3.8'                        - name: Install all dependencies        run: |          pip install -r requirements.txt                - name: Load Data        run: |          dvc repro dvc.yaml:load_data                - name: Split Data        run: |          dvc repro dvc.yaml:split_data                - name: Train and Evaluate        run: |          dvc repro dvc.yaml:train_and_evaluate                - name: Generate Report        run: |                    git fetch --prune          dvc metrics diff --show-md main > report.md          cml comment create report.mdname:ci-pipelineon: pushjobs:CI-Pipeline:runs-on:ubuntu-latestenv:repo_token:${{secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN}}steps: -name: Checkout Repouses:actions/checkout@v2 -name: Install CMLuses:iterative/setup-cml@v1 -name: Install DVCuses:iterative/setup-dvc@v1 -name: Setup pythonuses:actions/setup-python@v4with:python-version:'3.8' -name: Install all dependenciesrun:|          pip install -r requirements.txt -name: Load Datarun:|          dvc repro dvc.yaml:load_data -name: Split Datarun:|          dvc repro dvc.yaml:split_data -name: Train and Evaluaterun:|          dvc repro dvc.yaml:train_and_evaluate -name: Generate Reportrun:|                    git fetch --prune          dvc metrics diff --show-md main > report.md          cml comment create report.md. From checking out git repo, installing cml, dvc, python to installing all the required python packages and running all the stages mentioned in the dvc.yaml file and generating the reports with cml.

results.title: Stage 5.3. Experiment Tracking And Versioning — Omniverse
results.content: By tracking each experiment, data scientists can easily compare the results of different models, configurations, hyperparameters, and even completely different approaches. In addition to tracking experiments, it’s also important to version the models, code, and data used in those experiments. Tracking code can be easily done via version control systems like Git, and tracking data can be done via data versioning tools like DVC. Below we see some pseudo code on how to track the code, data, and model artifacts. DVC is designed to handle large data files, models, and metrics, and it integrates well with Git. DVC helps you track changes in your data files and manage different versions. * Run dvc checkout to update your data files to the version tracked at the specified commit. By combining code versioning with Git, data versioning with DVC, and logging artifacts and metadata with MLflow, you can ensure that your machine learning experiments are reproducible.
